title: A lane height under 8 pixels silently renders at the default 28
foundBy: session agent of a consuming timeline page, measuring a headless Chromium render; relayed by the repository owner

evidence.verified: The browser test that warns for a lane too short to draw passes. A lane of height 6 produces the warning naming the lane, the 8-pixel floor and the default 28. The TSDoc on `height` names the floor. `npm run ci` passes on 791cdaa, with every gate run. The visual gate passes 116 of 116 captures with no differing pixel and no new axe finding. The positioned fixture was re-recorded in 8566fe8. The dense, multi-lane and bar fixtures of the index layout are byte-identical to the baseline before this work. The build was served through `npm run registry:npmrevs` as 0.3.1-dev.20260922083722.8566fe8 and installed into the consuming dispatch viewer. That viewer's run14-1 render was measured in headless Chromium at 1500 by 1000.

resolution: A finite `height` under 8 still falls back to 28, and now says so in development, as an invalid span does. The prop's TSDoc names the floor.
details:
A finite `height` under 8 is replaced with 28, and nothing says so at the point of use. The TSDoc on `height` says only that the default is 28, and no development warning fires. The component document names the floor under its edge cases, and that document does not ship.

A consuming page asked for a 6-pixel gap lane, got a 28-pixel one, and the bands it had measured from its rows landed 22 pixels off. A height the component will not draw should be reported in development, as an invalid span is, and the floor should be named where the prop is declared.
